summary.text: 一 is a single horizontal stroke used for the numeral “one.” An oracle-bone example records it in the phrase “one ox.”

formation.text: Indicative: the horizontal stroke marks the abstract number one. It is a whole-graph analysis, not a compound of smaller parts.

history.text: The curated oracle-style and small-seal images each show a single horizontal stroke. They are modern redrawings of historical script styles, not artifact images, and do not establish a precise sequence of graphic changes.

The received Shuowen account gives 一 a cosmological role as the beginning from which heaven and earth are divided and the myriad things formed. This is a historical interpretation, not evidence that the graph depicted heaven or earth.
The dictionary labels 弌 an old form of 一. A proposed graphic derivation for 弌 is tentative, and no detailed transition from 弌 to 一 is established here.

uncertainties.text: The cited oracle-bone inscription has no supplied date, and a sequence of forms across periods is not established here.
The numeral analysis is supported; the proposal that 一 originally depicted heaven or earth is not. The chronology and development of the current senses “a/an” and “alone” remain unresolved.

senses.text: An oracle-bone example uses 一 in the numeral phrase “one ox.” This is an early attested use, not proof of the word’s hypothetical original meaning.
一 is also used with the present-day function “a, an.” Its date and development from the numeral sense are unresolved.
一 is also used with the present-day meaning “alone.” Its chronology and connection to the numeral sense are unresolved.

limitations.text: The oracle-bone example has no exact date. Current records list “a/an” and “alone” without historical dating, so no semantic transition is asserted.
